Subject: Follow-up: DPA incident notice expectations and evidence handover

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking my call earlier. FinServe is updating internal playbooks and we need to confirm how Redwood will handle the following if we ever have to invoke the DPA incident notification:

- 48-hour initial notification: what counts as the "initial notice" (email to a SOC/contact list, portal incident ticket, etc.)
- Evidence custody: who signs handover forms and what artifacts can be transferred vs. exported
- Subprocessor involvement: how Redwood will coordinate with third-party infra partners for forensics
- Retention during investigation: expected retention window for telemetry and raw logs while we validate

Can you confirm the practical steps and a point of contact for each? We may need to add a short clause to our contract to capture the handover flow.

Appreciate a concise run-through and any templates you can share.

Best,
Elena
Security Operations Manager
FinServe Inc.

Attachments: none
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA incident notice expectations and evidence handover

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I attached a short evidence-transfer matrix and the DPA excerpt related to notification windows for reference.

1) Initial 48-hour notification:
- What counts: an email to the customer SOC alias (security@finserv.com) or a ticket created in the Redwood incident portal (https://console.redwood.com/incidents) both qualify. We timestamp the notification and that timestamp is used for SLA calculations.
- Recommendation: prefer the security@ inbox for immediate legal/comms triage, then follow with the portal ticket for operational traceability.

2) Evidence custody and handover:
- Redwood will produce a forensic snapshot (timeboxed) and an evidence manifest. For export of raw disk images or custodial transfers we require a signed handover acknowledgement from an authorized FinServe liaison.
- Contact who signs: FinServe security lead or delegated SOC. If the request requires access to subprocessor logs, we coordinate with that subprocessors' liaison and copy you on the request.

3) Subprocessor coordination:
- We maintain a subprocessors roster and escalation chain; for forensic pulls we initiate a formal request and provide a timeline estimate within 24 hours. Some subprocessors impose export constraints — we'll document those in the evidence matrix.

4) Retention during investigation:
- Default: telemetry retained for 30 days hot, 90 days warm, with longer cold archives per contract. For active investigations we recommend preserving relevant slices for 180 days; we can do temporary holds on deletion with written confirmation.

Next steps: Ben (cc'd) will own building a concise handover checklist and custody form. Kimberly will confirm any SLA exceptions and run the redline with Legal. Marissa will scope the subprocessor notice language.

I'll follow up with a one-page playbook and the evidence matrix attached.

Thanks —
Soojin
Principal Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_matrix.xlsx, dpa_excerpt.pdf

Elena —

I've drafted a short custody acknowledgement template and an internal checklist (see attached runbook excerpt). Key practical notes:
- Signing authority: we need the name, title, and corporate email for the FinServe signee ahead of any custodial transfer. We can accept a signed PDF or DocuSign.
- Chain of custody: we log hashes and transfer receipts; if FinServe wants a physical handover window we can schedule a remote forensic session.
- Subprocessor artifacts: when a subprocessor is involved we will mark the item as "subproc-limited" and provide metadata describing constraints.

Propose a quick 30-min alignment call Wed 21 Jul 10am PT to walk the checklist. Can everyone confirm availability?

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Incident Ops (Redwood)

> - Chain of custody: we log hashes and transfer receipts; if FinServe wants a physical handover window we can schedule a remote forensic session.
> - Subprocessor artifacts: when a subprocessor is involved we will mark the item as "subproc-limited" and provide metadata describing constraints.

Elena — quick clarifications from Legal/Contracts side:
- 48-hour window: the DPA requires "prompt" notification; we map that to our 48-hour operational notice for incidents affecting Confidential Personal Data. The customer-facing notice is the security@ email.
- SLA exceptions: if export requires third-party approvals (e.g., cross-border subprocessors) we may propose a documented exception path; those exceptions are logged and timeboxed (typically +14 days).
- Evidence retention: we can put a temporary 180-day hold on identified slices with customer confirmation; permanent retention changes require a contract amendment.

I'll attach proposed contract language for the exception path and the short custody form. If FinServe is good with these, we'll produce a 1-page playbook and sign-off template for the signee.

—Kimberly
VP, Legal & Contracts (Redwood)

Attachments: custody_acknowledgement_template.pdf
